prompt: A bar graph shows the pets of $40$ students: dogs $16$, cats $12$, fish $7$, no pet $5$. What percent of the students have a dog?
hint: A percent compares a part with the whole group. Which number is the part here, and which is the whole?

hints.text: A percent compares a part with the whole group. Which number is the part here, and which is the whole?
The part is the $16$ dog owners and the whole is all $40$ students, so work out $\frac{16}{40}$ and turn it into a percent.
$\frac{16}{40} = 0.40$, so $40$ percent of the students have a dog.

explanation: The question asks about dog owners only, so the part is the $16$ students in the dog bar.
The whole is every student surveyed, which is $40$, so the relative frequency is $\frac{16}{40} = 0.40$.
Multiplying by $100$ turns the decimal into a percent, so $40$ percent of the students have a dog.

alternativeExplanations.title: Simplify the fraction first
steps: $\frac{16}{40}$ divides top and bottom by $8$ to give $\frac{2}{5}$.
$\frac{2}{5}$ of anything is $40$ percent — two of every five students.
